name: Explain a concept
summary: Help learners build a clear understanding of a concept they will later need to act on, judge or apply.
useWhen: The learner needs core understanding before using a concept in practice.
avoidWhen: Only one concise point needs to be retained; use Key message instead.
designGuidance: Organise the explanation around the understanding the learner needs, with clear hierarchy and readable density.
Use supporting visuals only when they add meaning.

definition.learnerNeed: Build the understanding needed for later action, judgement or application.

implementations.role: Present a straightforward explanation using native Rise content.
Group related explanatory content when a visible boundary helps comprehension.
Pair explanatory content with an image that adds meaning.

platformGuidance.rise: Prefer native image-and-text for straightforward explanations; use Split Card only where the image adds real meaning.

name: Key message
summary: Help the learner identify and retain one critical point.
useWhen: One legal threshold, definition or critical reminder needs deliberate emphasis.
avoidWhen: The content is routine supporting detail or contains more than one message.
designGuidance: Keep the message focused and concise, normally one to three sentences.
Treat its presentation as a recipe using Callout and typography, not as an independent canonical component.

definition.learnerNeed: Recognise and retain the single point that matters most in the current context.

implementations.role: Compose a focused message from Callout and typography.
implementations.note: This recipe is not an independent canonical component.

implementations.role: Provide emphasis within the Key message recipe.
Present a light-touch key message with a subheading and ordinary body text.

platformGuidance.rise: Use ordinary body text with a subheading when a separate visual treatment is unnecessary.

name: Explanatory feedback
summary: Help learners understand the reasoning and consequences behind a response and what to consider next.
useWhen: A learner response creates an opportunity to explain reasoning, consequences or a misconception.
avoidWhen: The response would only state correct or incorrect without useful reasoning.
designGuidance: Connect feedback directly to the learner's response and reveal it close to the action that caused it.
Explain consequences, address likely misconceptions and identify what the learner should consider next.
Choose an implementation suited to the activity; explanatory feedback is not limited to Decision Point.

definition.learnerNeed: Understand why a response is or is not appropriate, its likely consequences and how to improve the next judgement or action.

implementations.role: Provide explanatory feedback within a suitable native interaction.
Reveal explanatory feedback after a professional decision when that interaction is warranted.
implementations.note: Decision Point is one implementation, not the boundary of this purpose.

implementations.role: Present feedback revealed by a lightweight custom interaction.

platformGuidance.rise: Use the feedback capability of the chosen interaction and ensure dynamically revealed feedback is announced appropriately.

name: Reflection
summary: Help learners consider how learning relates to their own practice, experience or next action.
useWhen: A short reflective prompt or self-assessment genuinely helps transfer learning into practice.
avoidWhen: The prompt adds interaction or visual weight without supporting considered application.
A legacy Editorial Reflection treatment would be required.
designGuidance: Prefer native or lightweight reflection when a prompt alone provides sufficient support.
Use structured self-assessment only when ratings or criteria materially help the learner reflect.
Editorial Reflection is legacy and must not be recommended for new work.

definition.learnerNeed: Connect learning to personal practice or experience and consider an appropriate future action.

implementations.role: Present a concise reflection prompt with minimal interaction.
Give a lightweight reflection prompt an appropriate visual boundary.
Support a course-specific structured reflection using ratings or criteria.
implementations.note: Use only when a structured rating genuinely helps.

platformGuidance.rise: Prefer native statement or text blocks, or a compact Panel. Self-assessment is course-specific. Editorial Reflection remains legacy and is not recommended.

name: Contextualise a resource
summary: Help learners understand why a resource is relevant, where it leads and what they should do with it.
useWhen: A supplementary document or external guidance needs context before the learner opens it.
avoidWhen: Essential learning would be available only through the linked resource.
designGuidance: Name the resource, explain its relevance and identify the intended learner action.
Set clear expectations about the destination and what will happen when it opens.
Bring essential learning into the course rather than relying on an external destination.

definition.learnerNeed: Understand the relevance, destination and intended action associated with a supplementary resource.

implementations.role: Present a resource with context and a clear action.
Provide a lighter implementation when a card is unnecessary.

platformGuidance.rise: Use a native attachment or contextual text link for lighter cases; never rely on the link alone to provide essential learning.

name: Section opener
summary: Orient learners and support the transition into a meaningful new section.
useWhen: A major section genuinely begins and the learner needs orientation to its focus or purpose.
avoidWhen: Every heading or minor subtopic change is treated as a major transition.
designGuidance: Signal a meaningful structural transition and establish what the learner is moving into.
Keep orientation proportional to the importance of the section.

definition.structure: A distinct transition that introduces and orients the learner to a major section before its learning content begins.

implementations.role: Mark and orient a section transition using native Rise content.
Provide a designed section transition when stronger orientation is warranted.
implementations.note: The component is one possible implementation of the structure.

platformGuidance.rise: Choose a native banner or Section Opener component according to the strength of transition required.

name: Scenario stage
summary: Organise a continuing scenario into meaningful stages that preserve perspective, evidence and progression.
useWhen: A running scenario introduces a discrete context, update, observation or piece of evidence.
avoidWhen: The content is general explanation with no continuing scenario relationship.
designGuidance: Maintain a stable learner or decision-maker perspective across the scenario.
Make the relationship between each stage, new evidence and later progression clear.
Preserve continuity of the setting and situation while introducing only the evidence needed at that stage.

definition.structure: A sequence of connected scenario stages in which context or evidence develops from a consistent perspective and supports progression through the situation.

implementations.role: Present a discrete stage while maintaining visual and narrative continuity.
Arrange a lightweight continuing scenario using native content blocks.

platformGuidance.rise: Keep one stable visual environment and decision-maker perspective across the scenario, whether native blocks or the component are used.

name: Ordered sequence
summary: Organise actions or stages where genuine order, dependencies or progression matter to understanding or outcome.
useWhen: Actions, dependencies, stages or progression have a meaningful order.
avoidWhen: Items are not truly sequential and a list or grid would communicate them more honestly.
designGuidance: Make the reason for the order clear, including dependencies or changes between stages.
Use numbering only where the number carries meaning.

definition.structure: An ordered organisation of actions or stages whose sequence, dependencies or progression are significant.

implementations.role: Present a straightforward ordered sequence using native content.
Present a designed sequence where its stages benefit from stronger visual organisation.

platformGuidance.rise: Use native ordered content when it is sufficient; use Process when stronger staged organisation supports comprehension.

name: Comparison structure
summary: Organise related roles, responses or alternatives so learners can identify straightforward similarities and differences.
useWhen: A small number of related items can be compared through clear, parallel categories.
avoidWhen: The content is too extensive for a clear comparison or the activity requires a more sophisticated evaluate-and-decide experience.
designGuidance: Keep comparison categories parallel and make important differences explicit.
Choose an organisation suited to the content volume and the number of alternatives.
More sophisticated compare–evaluate–decide learning activity requires additional learning design and is not defined by this structure alone.

definition.structure: A parallel organisation of a manageable set of related items under consistent categories to make simple similarities and differences clear.

implementations.role: Compare two related roles or positions through parallel categories.
Present a compact comparison in rows and columns.
Organise alternatives as cards when side-by-side scanning is useful.
Separate comparison categories when the content benefits from guided navigation.

platformGuidance.rise: Select Role Split, a table, Card Grid or category navigation according to the content; the structure does not prescribe one treatment.

name: Section summary
summary: Provide meaningful closure to a major section and reinforce the learning before transition.
useWhen: A major section ends and the learner benefits from deliberate closure and reinforcement.
avoidWhen: Every subtopic is followed by a summary regardless of its significance.
designGuidance: Reinforce the most important learning in a concise set of points.
Use the summary to close the section and prepare the learner for a genuine transition.

definition.structure: A deliberate closing segment that consolidates a major section's learning and marks the transition away from it.

implementations.role: Close a section with concise native text or list content.
Give a major section a strong visual close when warranted.
implementations.note: Footer Band is one possible implementation, not a requirement.

platformGuidance.rise: Use three to five concise points where appropriate. Choose Footer Band only when a deliberate visual close is useful.

name: Legislation or authority
summary: Express authoritative material so learners can distinguish the source from explanation and understand its implications for action.
useWhen: A specific Act, regulation, section or other authority underpins a requirement.
avoidWhen: A general policy statement has no identified authoritative source.
designGuidance: Identify the authority precisely and keep authoritative material visibly separate from explanation.
Use plain-language interpretation where appropriate and make the learner implication or action explicit.
Use extracts and citations carefully, retaining enough context for accurate interpretation.
Treat the expression as a recipe supported by Split Card and typography, not as an independent canonical Legislation Panel component.

definingFeatures: An accurately identified authority or source.
Clear separation between authoritative material and explanation.
An explicit learner implication or action.
Careful, contextual use of extracts and citations.

implementations.role: Compose authoritative source material, explanation and learner implications using Split Card and typography.
implementations.note: Legislation Panel is not an independent canonical component.

implementations.role: Support visible separation between the authority and its explanation.
Present a lighter expression when typography and clear source labelling are sufficient.

platformGuidance.rise: Use Split Card or native text according to content needs while preserving source accuracy, separation and learner implications.

name: Professional decision point
summary: Give learners credible practice in making a meaningful professional choice or judgement and understanding its reasoning or consequences.
useWhen: A credible professional situation presents plausible alternatives and the learner benefits from practising judgement.
avoidWhen: The learner problem is only recall or confirmation, or alternatives would be obviously implausible.
designGuidance: Ground the decision in a credible professional situation and present a meaningful choice or judgement.
Use plausible alternatives that reflect realistic reasoning, not superficial distractors.
Explain the reasoning or consequence and provide explanatory feedback after the choice.
Use the expression for practice rather than simple recall.

definingFeatures: Reasoning or consequence connected to the choice.

implementations.role: Provide an interactive professional choice with revealed reasoning and feedback.
implementations.note: Decision Point is one possible interactive implementation.

implementations.role: Handle recall or confirmation when a professional decision expression is not needed.
implementations.note: This is an alternative for a simpler learner problem, not an implementation of professional judgement.

platformGuidance.rise: Use Decision Point for credible professional judgement. Use a native knowledge check when the learner problem is only recall or confirmation.
